claims.claim: REMOVED, the sweep's worst finding on this page (F-FAIL) and WORSE THAN THE SWEEP RECORDED: "enacted with minimal floor attention - it passed by unanimous consent in both chambers, reflecting bipartisan agreement on both the extension and the security screening provisions." The sweep flagged the House half only. Both halves are wrong. Congress.gov records the Senate as having "passed without amendment by Voice Vote" on 2026-03-03 and the House as "On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 345 - 41 (Roll no. 89)" on 2026-03-17. "Minimal floor attention" is contradicted by the same record: forty minutes of House debate on 2026-03-16 and a demand for the yeas and nays. The motive clause ("reflecting bipartisan agreement") was unsourced and went with it. Replaced with the record, and with the voice-vote/unanimous-consent distinction in the house style set by the freshly audited unanimous-consent.html, which this paragraph now links.

REMOVED, F-FAIL: "Phase I provides initial feasibility funding (up to $200,000 for six months); Phase II funds full development (up to $1.5 million for two years)." Neither figure is in S. 3971 - the only dollar amounts in the whole Act are $30,000,000, $100,000,000, $6,500 and $50,000 - and neither is in 15 U.S.C. 638. The statutory guideline amounts are $150,000 for Phase I and $1,000,000 for Phase II, adjusted for inflation every year, with greater or lesser amounts at the awarding agency's discretion. The six-month Phase I duration is in no source at all; the statute gives durations only for STTR (1-year Phase I, 2-year Phase II). Replaced with the statutory guideline, the inflation-adjustment mechanic, the agency-discretion clause, and the observed spread on the article's own cited source, SBIR.gov. A current-year inflation-adjusted figure was deliberately NOT published: sbir.gov/faqs returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-01, so there is no stored source for one.

REMOVED, F-FAIL: "The eight watchlists specified in the bill include the Treasury Department's Specially Designated Nationals list, the Commerce Department's Entity List and Unverified List, and several Defense and intelligence community lists." Three errors in one sentence. The Treasury list the Act names is the Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List - Non-SDN means the opposite of the SDN list. There is no Unverified List among the eight. No intelligence-community list is among them either, and 15 U.S.C. 638(e)(2) expressly excludes any Intelligence Community agency from the definition of "Federal agency" for this section. The sentence also omitted the DHS, FCC and CBP lists entirely. Replaced with all eight, quoted from the Act with the maintaining agency the Act itself names.

REMOVED, F-FAIL that the sweep did not catch: "to identify ties to foreign adversaries - defined to include China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea, among others." The phrase "foreign adversary" does not occur anywhere in S. 3971, and neither do "China", "Russia", "Iran" or "North Korea". The term the underlying statute defines is "foreign country of concern" at 15 U.S.C. 638(e)(17), which does name those four countries plus any other the Secretary of State designates - but that term governs the due diligence provisions, not the eight-list ground, which has no country condition. Replaced with the statutory term, its statutory definition, and an explicit statement of which provision it governs.

REMOVED, F-UNSOURCED (two claims): "The programs collectively distribute billions of dollars annually" and "The Department of Defense alone has set aside more than $1 billion per year for SBIR grants." Neither "venture capital", "national of" nor "principal" occurs in the Act. The nearest real provisions are 638(g)(13)(E), which requires DISCLOSURE of venture-capital or institutional investment where a general partner or leader has a foreign affiliation with a foreign country of concern, and the 638(vv)(2)(A) due-diligence list the Act rewrites, which turns on foreign ownership and financial ties rather than nationality. REMOVED, F-UNSOURCED definition: "STTR grants require a partnership between a small business and a research institution (a university or federal lab)." The statute defines the partner as a "nonprofit institution, as defined in section 3703(5)" of title 15, a definition that "includes federally funded research and development centers" - it does not say university, and an FFRDC is not the same thing as a federal lab. The statute also fixes the split, which the article never mentioned: not less than 40 percent of the work by the small business and not less than 30 percent by the research institution. REMOVED, F-FAIL arithmetic: "S. 3971 extended both programs through fiscal year 2031, providing five years of certainty for applicants and agencies planning their R&D budgets." The Act moves the date from September 30, 2025 to September 30, 2031. That is six additional fiscal years, FY2026 through FY2031, not five. Replaced with both dates and the count.

REMOVED, F-UNSOURCED: "Applicants are required to certify compliance; agencies are required to verify against the watchlists before making awards." The word "certify" does not appear anywhere in S. 3971. The Act imposes duties on agencies - evaluate, deny, notify, examine - and the applicant-facing requirement it relies on is the pre-existing DISCLOSURE list at 638(g)(13). Replaced with the Act's own verbs.
